title: Understanding Artificial Intelligence

description.main: An illustrated 1985 introduction to artificial intelligence by Henry C. Mishkoff, with a foreword by Edward A. Feigenbaum. It covers symbolic processing, expert systems and natural language processing, with interviews with AI researchers.
description.extended:
An illustrated primer on artificial intelligence from 1985, written for general readers and published in the Sams Understanding Series with the Texas Instruments Learning Center.

The book explains what artificial intelligence is, what it is used for and what effect it may have on daily life. It covers symbolic processing, expert systems, natural language processing and applications. Edward A. Feigenbaum wrote the foreword. Interviews and contributions come from AI researchers including Bruce Buchanan, Randall Davis, Mark Fox, Douglas Lenat, David McDonald, Ronald Ohlander and Harry Tennant. The Texas Instruments Information Publishing Center staff developed it. It has 258 pages, a bibliography and an index.

Henry C. Mishkoff is the author. A second edition revised by Dan Shafer and Daniel W. Rasmus followed in 1988 (H.W. Sams, ISBN 9780672272714).

notes: Catalogued as the Howard W. Sams edition (ISBN 9780672270215, 1985; Open Library and the LC record give 1985, one AbeBooks listing gives 1986; also sold through Radio Shack).
